sources.note: Benchmarks 20-plus models as MQM translation-quality judges, finds reasoning models best and a jury of different ones better than any member, then distils that jury's agreement-filtered annotations into a 12B student that beats every open reasoning-model judge tested.
sources.title: TQLite: Multi-LLM Jury Guided Distillation for Real-time MQM Translation Quality Evaluation

sources.note: Measures not how far six frontier models move under steering pressure but what kind of response they give when they decline, finds several response modes belonging to a single model, and then traces the largest within-model split to a linearly decodable and causally steerable direction in an open-weight model's residual stream.
sources.title: Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models Under Steering Pressure

sources.note: Puts an ensemble of LLM judges between a robot-autonomy planner and its execution layer as gating middleware that accepts, rejects or escalates each plan to human review, and reports that ensemble size barely moves accuracy while the errors concentrate at the escalate boundary rather than between accept and reject.
sources.title: Agentic Harnesses: LLM-Driven Verification Layers for Robot Autonomy

sources.note: Structures multi-agent medical differential diagnosis as rounds of persona-conditioned specialist deliberation, and shows the recall advantage is not reproduced by best-of-n sampling from the same model, concentrates entirely in the cases where monolithic inference fails, and reverses on the easiest quartile.
sources.title: Social Chain of Thought: A Multi-Agent Architecture Grounded in Medical Differential Diagnosis Methodology

result.definition: Combining several model judges rather than trusting one, and across 4 sources a remedy for judge unreliability whose returns the corpus finds are uneven. The positive case: a jury of different models is better than any member on translation quality, and its agreement-filtered annotations distil into a 12B student that beats every open reasoning-model judge tested -- with the authors noting the filter may be removing exactly the edge cases a judge most needs to see. The negative case is equally specific: in a robot-autonomy verification harness, ensemble size barely moves accuracy while the errors concentrate at the escalate boundary rather than between accept and reject, so adding judges buys nothing where the difficulty is deciding what needs a human. A third source finds several response modes belonging to a single model under steering pressure, which bears on aggregation directly -- within-model variance can exceed between-model variance, so an ensemble of one model's samples and an ensemble of different models are not the same instrument. And one multi-agent deliberation study finds its advantage concentrating entirely in cases where single-model inference fails and reversing on the easiest quartile.
